title_ar: حكم من أقيمت عليه الصلاة وهو في نافلة
title_en: The ruling on one for whom the prayer is called while he is in a voluntary prayer
body_ar:
ما حكم المتنفل إذا أقيمت الفريضة عليه هل يأتي بباقيها جالسا أم لا؟

أن النبي (ص) قال: «إذا أقيمت الصلاة فلا صلاة إلا المكتوبة» وهذا الحديث ثابت عن النبي (ص) فليس البحث إذن في صحته إنما البحث في دلالته، وقد اختلف أهل العلم في دلالته، فذهب بعضهم إلى أن معنى قوله: لا صلاة، أي لا استئناف صلاة، وذهب آخرون إلى أن معناها لا صحة صلاة، واتفق الجميع على أن لا نافية لا ناهية، لأن لا الناهية لا تدخل على الاسم هنا بل لو كان لا بمعنى النهي لقال: فلا تصلوا، إذا أقيمت الصلاة فلا تصلوا لكن قال: لا صلاة، ولا نافية إذن والنفي لا ينصب على وجود الصلاة لأن ذلك كذب فنحن نشاهد الصلاة وقد أقيمت الفريضة والنبي (ص) يستحيل الكذب في حقه فدل ذلك على أن ثم مقتضى محذوفا لا يستقيم الكلام إلا به، وهذه الدلالة هي التي تسمى لدى الأصوليين بدلالة الاقتضاء..

وهي أن ثم محذوفا لا يستقيم الكلام إلا به، وهذا المحذوف الذي هو المقتضى لا عموم له، لا يمكن أن يكون يشمل عددا من الاحتمالات بل لا بد أن يحصر في احتمال واحد، فهنا هذا المحذوف الذي لا يستقيم الكلام إلا به ثلاثة أقسام، القسم الأول ما لا يستقيم الكلام عقلا إلا به، وذلك مثل قول الله تعالى: {وَكَانَ وَرَاءَهُمْ مَلِكٌ يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ غَصْبًا (79)} [الكهف]، فالكلام هنا لا يستقيم عقلا إلا بمحذوف لأن خرق السفينة لا يخرجها عن أن تكون سفينة فهو خرقها وقال بعد ذلك {وَكَانَ وَرَاءَهُمْ مَلِكٌ يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ غَصْبًا (79)} هل خرقها يخرجها عن كونها سفينة، لا يخرجها عن كونها سفينة، إذن لا بد من محذوف تقديره كل سفينة صالحة، لأن الملك لا يأخذ إلا السفن الصالحة، فلذلك خرق الخضر السفينة حتى يكون فيها عيب تنجو من الملك بسببه، إذن هذا المحذوف الذي لا يستقيم الكلام عقلا إلا به، النوع الثاني لا تستقيم صحة الكلام إلا به يكون الكلام كذبا بدونه، وذلك مثل قول النبي (ص): رفع لي عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان وما استكرهوا عليه فالخطأ والنسيان موجودان في الأمة والاستكراه موجود في الأمة فإذن لا يستقيم الكلام إلا بمحذوف تقديره إثم الخطإ والنسيان وما استكرهوا عليه، فالمرفوع عن الأمة هو إثم الخطإ والنسيان وما استكرهوا عليه، لا وجود الخطإ والنسيان وما استكرهوا عليه فهذا موجود، القسم الثالث ما لا يستقيم معناه شرعا إلا بذلك المحذوف، وذلك مثل قولك تصدق عني بكذا تصدق عني بدارك، فأنا لا يمكن أن أتصدق عنك إلا أن تملك أنت الدار ثم أتصدق عنك بها لأن المقصود بالصدقة عنك إخراجها بعد أن تدخل ملكك، فمعنى هذا بعني دارك أو أعطني دارك ثم تصدق بها عني، فإذن ثم محذوف لا يستقيم الكلام إلا به شرعا فقط لا عقلا، ومن هنا فإن قوله (ص): «إذا أقيمت الصلاة فلا صلاة إلا المكتوبة» من هذا القبيل، فحمله بعض أهل العلم على أن المقصود به: لا إتمام صلاة فرأوا أن الإنسان إذا كان متنفلا فأقيمت عليه الصلاة وهو في المسجد فعليه أن يقطع تلك النافلة ليشترك مع الإمام في الصلاة، فقد قال النبي (ص): أصلاتان معا لما رأى بعض الناس يصلي والإمام يصلي، وقالت طائفة أخرى بل المحذوف الذي لا يستقيم الكلام دونه تقديره فلا استئناف صلاة، فإذا أقيمت الصلاة لا يحل للإنسان أن يحرم من جديد بصلاة أخرى في المسجد، وهذا الذي أخذ به جمهور أهل العلم، ويرجع هذا الخلاف إلى خلاف آخر هو الخلاف في النفل هل يجب بالشروع أم لا؟ فنحن نعلم أن الشارع لما شرع الأحكام لم يجعلها على درجة واحدة، قد جعل بعضها واجبا وبعضها مندوبا، وحكمة الشارع أن يبقى الواجب على الوجوب والمندوب على الندب، لكن بعد الشروع فيه قد اختلف فيه أهل العلم، فقالت طائفة منهم: يجب النفل بالشروع، وقالت طائفة: لا يجب النفل بالشروع، وخرج من الخلاف أمران، الأمر الأول ما اتفق على وجوبه بالشروع وهو الحج والعمرة، فمن أحرم بحج أو عمرة متنفلا فإنه يجب عليه إكمالهما ولا يحل له قطعهما إجماعا، والأمر الثاني هو ما يحل قطعه مطلقا، لا يجب بالشروع عند الجميع وهو الطهارة والوقف، فالإنسان إذا بدأ يتوضأ ثم بدا له أن ينام يحل له قطع وضوئه، وإذا أراد أن يغتسل ثم بدا له أن يخرج لحاجة فيحل له قطع غسله وهذا محل اتفاق بين أهل العلم، ومثل ذلك الوقف إذا وقف الإنسان دارا ثم بدا له أن يتراجع عن الوقف فيحل له ذلك، فإذن هذا الأمر الثاني المستثنى هما خارجان عن محل الخلاف، يبقى محل الخلاف فيما عدا ذلك إذا أحرم الإنسان بصلاة نافلة فالأصل عدم وجوبها، ولكن الشروع أدخله في حريم الصلاة، فهل يجب عليه إكمالها أم لا؟ ذهب مالك وأبو حنيفة إلى أن النفل يجب بالشروع، وذهب الشافعي وأحمد إلى أن النفل لا يجب بالشروع، على القول بوجوب النفل بالشروع فإن الإنسان إذا شرع في الصلاة ولو كانت نافلة لا يحل له قطعها لفريضة أقيمت لأنه قد تلبس بفرض فلا يخرج من فرض إلى فرض آخر، وهذا مذهب مالك وأبي حنيفة واستدلا بقول الله تعالى: {وَلَا تُبْطِلُوا أَعْمَالَكُمْ (33)}[محمد] وذهب الشافعي وأحمد إلى أن النفل لا يلزم بالشروع فحكمة الشارع تقتضي التمييز بين ما هو واجب وما هو مندوب، فما أوجبه الشارع يبقى على وجوبه، وما جعله مندوبا يبقى على ندبه، وعلى هذا لا يجب عندهم النفل بالشروع فيجوز للإنسان الذي أحرم بنافلة أن يقطعها لأي سبب من الأسباب، والشافعي يرى جواز التنفل بالركعة الواحدة، إذا أحرم الإنسان فأتى بركعة فأقيمت الصلاة يجوز له أن يتشهد ويسلم عند الشافعي، لكن مع ذلك فالمالكية مراعاة للخلاف يرون أن عليه أن يتجوز فيها لأن النبي (ص) ذكر التجوز في الصلاة في الركعتين في وقت خطبة الإمام على المنبر كما في حديث أبي هريرة «إذا دخل أحدكم المسجد يوم الجمعة والإمام يخطب فلا يجلس حتى يصلي ركعتين وليتجوز فيهما» وليتجوز فيهما معناه ليقصرهما يقصر قراءتهما وركوعهما وسجودهما، فرأوا أنه يتجوز فيهما، وهذا التجوز يشمل الجلوس إذا كانت حركاته أخف في حال الجلوس فيكمل الركعتين جالسا، وذهب بعض أهل العلم إلى التفصيل، فقالوا: إذا كان قد أتم ركعة فعليه أن يشفعها بأخرى، أما إذا كان في الركعة الأولى فيقطعها، وهذا قول لبعض المالكية، يرون أنه إذا لم يعقد الركوع يقطع وإذا كان قد عقد الركوع أتمها بركعة أخرى شفعها بركعة أخرى وشفع إن ركع كما قال خليل رحمه الله، وهذا تفصيل في هذه المسألة والبحث فيها يرجع إلى الفقه والأصول معا، فما يتعلق منه بإيجاب النفل بالشروع بحث أصولي، وما يتعلق بإكمال النافلة بعد إقامة الصلاة في المسجد بحث فقهي.
body_en:
What is the ruling on one performing a voluntary prayer when the obligatory prayer is called while he is in it? Does he perform the rest of it sitting, or not?

The Prophet, upon whom be peace, said: "When the prayer is called, there is no prayer but the prescribed one." This hadith is established from the Prophet, upon whom be peace, so the investigation is not into its soundness but into its signification; and the people of knowledge differed as to its signification. Some of them held that the meaning of his words "there is no prayer" is "there is no beginning afresh of a prayer", and others held that its meaning is "there is no validity of a prayer". All agreed that the lā is a negating lā and not a prohibiting one, because the prohibiting lā does not enter upon a noun here — rather, had lā been in the sense of prohibition he would have said "so do not pray": "when the prayer is called, do not pray". But he said "there is no prayer". So the lā is negating; and the negation is not directed at the existence of the prayer, because that would be untrue, for we see the prayer taking place when the obligatory prayer has been called, and untruth is impossible in the case of the Prophet, upon whom be peace. That indicates that there is an elided element required by the sense, without which the speech does not stand. This signification is what the legal theorists call the signification of requirement (dalālat al-iqtiḍāʾ)..

It is that there is an elided element without which the speech does not stand; and this elided element, which is the thing required, has no generality — it cannot comprise a number of possibilities, but must be confined to a single possibility.

Here, this elided element without which the speech does not stand is of three kinds. The first kind: that without which the speech does not stand rationally, as in God Most High's words: {And there was behind them a king seizing every ship by force (79)} [al-Kahf]. The speech here does not stand rationally except by an elided element, because making a hole in the ship does not take it out of being a ship. He made a hole in it, and then He said {And there was behind them a king seizing every ship by force (79)}. Does making a hole in it take it out of being a ship? It does not take it out of being a ship. So there must be an elided element, its implied sense being "every sound ship", because the king took only sound ships — which is why al-Khidr made a hole in the ship, so that there might be a defect in it by reason of which it would escape the king. This, then, is the elided element without which the speech does not stand rationally.

The second kind: that without which the correctness of the speech does not stand — the speech would be untrue without it. That is like the Prophet's words, upon whom be peace: "Error, and forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to, have been lifted for me from my community." For error and forgetfulness exist in the community, and compulsion exists in the community; so the speech does not stand except by an elided element, its implied sense being "the sin of error, and of forgetfulness, and of what they are compelled to". What has been lifted from the community is the sin of error and forgetfulness and what they are compelled to — not the existence of error and forgetfulness and what they are compelled to, for this exists.

The third kind: that whose meaning does not stand in the eyes of the Sharia except by that elided element. That is like your saying "give in charity on my behalf with such-and-such", "give in charity on my behalf with your house". For I cannot give in charity on your behalf unless you own the house and I then give it in charity on your behalf, because what is meant by charity on your behalf is its being given out after it has entered your ownership. So the meaning of this is "sell me your house", or "give me your house and then give it in charity on my behalf". So there is an elided element without which the speech does not stand in the eyes of the Sharia only, and not rationally.

From here, his words, upon whom be peace, "When the prayer is called, there is no prayer but the prescribed one", are of this sort. Some of the people of knowledge took them to mean "there is no completing of a prayer", and so held that if a person is performing a voluntary prayer and the prayer is called while he is in the mosque, he must break off that voluntary prayer in order to join with the imam in the prayer — for the Prophet, upon whom be peace, said: "Two prayers together?", when he saw some people praying while the imam was praying. And another group said: rather, the elided element without which the speech does not stand is to be taken as "so there is no beginning afresh of a prayer" — so that when the prayer is called it is not lawful for a person to enter anew upon another prayer in the mosque. This is what the majority of the people of knowledge adopted.

This disagreement goes back to another disagreement, namely the disagreement as to the voluntary act: does it become obligatory by commencing it, or not? For we know that when the Lawgiver legislated the rulings, He did not put them all at one degree: He made some of them obligatory and some of them recommended; and the wisdom of the Lawgiver is that the obligatory should remain at obligation and the recommended at recommendation. But as to after commencing it, the people of knowledge have differed. One group of them said: the voluntary becomes obligatory by commencement. Another group said: the voluntary does not become obligatory by commencement.

Two matters fall outside the disagreement. The first matter is that which is agreed to become obligatory by commencement, namely the hajj and the lesser pilgrimage: whoever enters the consecrated state for a voluntary hajj or lesser pilgrimage is obliged to complete them, and it is not lawful for him to break them off, by consensus. The second matter is that which it is lawful to break off without qualification, which does not become obligatory by commencement in anyone's view, namely ritual purification and endowment. If a person begins to perform ablution and it then occurs to him to sleep, it is lawful for him to break off his ablution; and if he intends to perform the full ritual washing and it then occurs to him to go out for some need, it is lawful for him to break off his washing — and this is a point of agreement among the people of knowledge. The like of that is endowment: if a person endows a house and it then occurs to him to go back on the endowment, that is lawful for him. So this second excepted matter — the two of them are outside the locus of the disagreement.

The locus of the disagreement remains in what is besides that. If a person enters the consecrated state for a voluntary prayer, the base rule is that it is not obligatory; but the commencing of it has brought him within the sanctuary of the prayer. So is he obliged to complete it, or not? Malik and Abu Hanifah held that the voluntary becomes obligatory by commencement, and al-Shafi'i and Ahmad held that the voluntary does not become obligatory by commencement.

On the view that the voluntary becomes obligatory by commencement, if a person has commenced the prayer — even a voluntary one — it is not lawful for him to break it off for an obligatory prayer that has been called, because he has already clothed himself in an obligation, and one does not pass out of one obligation into another obligation. This is the school of Malik and Abu Hanifah, and the two of them argued from God Most High's words: {And do not nullify your deeds (33)} [Muhammad].

And al-Shafi'i and Ahmad held that the voluntary is not made binding by commencement, for the wisdom of the Lawgiver requires a distinction between what is obligatory and what is recommended: what the Lawgiver made obligatory remains at its obligation, and what He made recommended remains at its recommendation. On this, the voluntary does not in their view become obligatory by commencement, so it is permissible for a person who has entered the consecrated state for a voluntary prayer to break it off for any of the reasons. And al-Shafi'i holds it permissible to perform a voluntary prayer of a single rakʿah: if a person has entered the consecrated state and performed one rakʿah, and the prayer is then called, it is permissible for him to say the tashahhud and give the salām, according to al-Shafi'i.

Even so, the Malikis, out of regard for the disagreement, hold that he must abbreviate it, because the Prophet, upon whom be peace, mentioned abbreviating the prayer in the two rakʿahs at the time of the imam's sermon upon the pulpit, as in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "When one of you enters the mosque on Friday and the imam is delivering the sermon, let him not sit until he has prayed two rakʿahs, and let him abbreviate them." "And let him abbreviate them" means: let him shorten them — he shortens their recitation, their bowing and their prostration. So they held that he abbreviates them; and this abbreviating extends to sitting, if his movements are lighter in the sitting position, so that he completes the two rakʿahs sitting.

And some of the people of knowledge went to a detailed distinction, and said: if he has completed a rakʿah, he must pair it with another; but if he is in the first rakʿah, he breaks it off. This is a view of some of the Malikis: they hold that if he has not fixed the bowing he breaks it off, and if he has fixed the bowing he completes it with another rakʿah — he pairs it with another rakʿah; "and pair, if he has bowed", as Khalil, may God have mercy on him, said.

This is a detailed distinction in this question, and the investigation of it goes back to fiqh and to legal theory together: what pertains in it to the voluntary being made obligatory by commencement is an investigation in legal theory, and what pertains to completing the voluntary prayer after the prayer has been called in the mosque is an investigation in fiqh.

flags.context: وهذه الدلالة هي التي تسمى لدى الأصوليين بدلالة الاقتضاء
flags.note: A central term of legal theory that is not in the project glossary, and the whole first half of this text is an exposition of it. It denotes the meaning a text carries by way of a word that must be supplied for the text to be true or intelligible. 'Implied meaning' is too loose and would be confused with dalālat al-ishārah and the other significations, which are distinct categories. The term and its siblings should be added to the glossary before more usul material is translated.

flags.arabic: فأنا لا يمكن أن أتصدق عنك إلا أن تملك أنت الدار ثم أتصدق عنك بها
flags.context: the third kind of elided element: the example of asking someone to give his house in charity on one's behalf
options: translate as printed, with the pronouns as they stand
translate on the reading that the roles are reversed here, to match the example and the conclusion
flags.note: PRONOUN CONFUSION IN THE SOURCE. The example is given as 'give in charity on MY behalf with YOUR house' and the conclusion returns to that framing ('sell me your house, or give me your house and then give it in charity on my behalf'). But the sentence between them inverts the roles: 'I cannot give in charity on YOUR behalf unless YOU own the house'. As the example is set up, the requirement is that the speaker, not the addressee, must first own the house. This is almost certainly the Sheikh switching viewpoint mid-explanation in speech, as happens constantly in a lecture, rather than a doctrinal statement; the underlying point — that ownership must transfer first — is the same either way and is unaffected. Translated as printed under the rule against silently repairing the source. Option 2 is set out only to be rejected.

flags.arabic: ومثل ذلك الوقف إذا وقف الإنسان دارا ثم بدا له أن يتراجع عن الوقف فيحل له ذلك
flags.context: endowment given as an example of an act that does not become binding by commencement
options: translate as printed and attach a display caveat
translate as printed with no caveat
gloss in the body that what is meant is an endowment not yet completed
flags.note: HIGH RISK OF MISREADING, and the reason this record is marked critical_for_display. Read on its own, the sentence says that a man who has endowed a house may go back on the endowment — which is not the settled position on a completed waqf, where irrevocability is close to a point of consensus. In context the Sheikh is plainly discussing the effect of COMMENCING an act, not of completing one, and is listing purification and endowment as acts that do not bind merely by being begun. But a reader who reaches this page through a search for waqf will land on a bare sentence appearing to permit revocation. Option 2 would insert the Sheikh's premise into his words. The right remedy is a display caveat, or a pull-quote guard, not a change to the text.

flags.arabic: رفع لي عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان وما استكرهوا عليه
flags.context: the hadith cited as the second kind of elided element
options: translate as printed, 'have been lifted FOR ME from my community'
read as the received wording, 'have been lifted from my community', without 'for me'
note the variant and translate as printed
flags.note: The report is commonly cited as rufiʿa ʿan ummatī al-khaṭaʾ wa-l-nisyān wa-mā ustukrihū ʿalayh. The source has rufiʿa lī ʿan ummatī, adding 'for me'. That wording is attested in some transmissions, so this is not necessarily an error; but since the Sheikh is using the report for a precise grammatical point about what the verb governs, the reviewer should know the extra word is there. Translated as printed.

flags.context: the Malikis' position that he should abbreviate the prayer
options: the Malikis, out of regard for the disagreement
the Malikis, taking account of the difference of opinion
the Malikis, by way of precaution
flags.note: Murāʿāt al-khilāf is a named and distinctively Maliki principle: giving some legal effect to the view one does not oneself hold, out of regard for the fact that it is held. It is not the same as precaution (iḥtiyāṭ), which option 2 would suggest, and it is not a mere gesture of politeness towards other schools. The term is not in the glossary and should be added, since it is a hallmark of the school this corpus belongs to.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

THE SHEIKH DOES NOT GIVE HIS OWN RULING IN THIS TEXT. He sets out the disagreement between Malik and Abu Hanifah on one side and al-Shafi'i and Ahmad on the other, then reports al-Shafi'i's position on a single-rakʿah voluntary prayer, then the Maliki position on abbreviating, then a detailed distinction held by 'some of the Malikis', and closes by classifying the question rather than answering it. The last position stated — the Maliki detail, with the line from Khalil — is therefore NOT his fatwa, and the page must not be laid out so that it reads as one. The questioner's actual question, whether the remainder is performed sitting, is touched only within the report of the Maliki view on abbreviating.

The double dot at the end of the first paragraph is in the source and marks the CMS 'intro text' break; the text continues below it and is not truncated. No download link is offered and the text ends on a completed sentence, so this record is not an excerpt.

'The signification of requirement' and its three kinds are the argumentative spine of the text and have been preserved as a chain in full. Compressing the three kinds into their conclusion would remove the whole reason the Sheikh gives this answer at this length.

'The prescribed one' renders al-maktūbah, the obligatory prayer. 'The consecrated state' renders iḥrām, used here of entering the state of prayer by the opening takbīr as well as of the pilgrimage — the Arabic uses the one word for both, and the English keeps it so because the Sheikh's argument moves between the two cases.
'The sanctuary of the prayer' renders ḥarīm al-ṣalāh, the protected precinct of the act, which commencement brings a person within.
'He has clothed himself in an obligation' renders talabbasa bi-farḍ.
'Fixed the bowing' renders ʿaqada al-rukūʿ, the point at which the bowing is settled and counts.
Khalil is Khalil ibn Ishaq al-Jundi, whose Mukhtaṣar is the standard reference text of the Maliki school; 'and pair, if he has bowed' is a quotation from it.

The verse references are given by the source itself in the form it uses — verse number in the text and sura name in square brackets — and that form has been preserved rather than converted to house style, because here the source supplies the reference and elsewhere in this slice it does not.

The paragraph breaks in body_en beyond those in body_ar are editorial. The source runs the second half of this text as one very long paragraph; it has been broken in the English at the turns of the argument only, and body_ar is as served.
